hypothesis: The parent's failures are (a) final '?' fills that contradict the task rules (in 26/30 circuits the parent's own 18 answers already admit exactly one rule-consistent table, yet only 11/30 were right) and (b) queries spent on rows the rules already force (zero_info ~0.4), which left the remaining circuits as 2-way ties. If the harness derives the rule-consistent tables from the system-prompt rules + answers, vetoes forced-answer queries like repeats, shows the forced rows / candidates at the final turn and snaps each circuit to the nearest consistent table, exact-table accuracy on this batch rises from 10% to >=90% with the model still writing every query.
behavior_changes: New rule-derived enumerator (_tables / consistent): per circuit, the 8-bit tables buildable from two 2-input gates (g=op1(xi,xj), out=op2(g,xk)) with stackable NOTs on any of the 5 signals, non-constant, under some split of the inventory that fits all circuits' answers. Built only from the system-prompt rules, inventory and env.history.
veto_reason: a query whose answer is already forced by the rules is vetoed (no query spent), with a message listing every still-uncertain row per circuit.
Share cap (ceil(B/3)) only vetoes when some other circuit still has open rows and is under its cap.
Query loop stops early once every row of every circuit is forced.
Final prompt appends 'Deduced from the rules:' (fully determined table, or candidate list + forced rows) after the parent's observed table.

assemble(): also reads per-circuit 8-digit lines ('Circuit A: 00010101') when the 24-bit string is malformed (the 7B dropped digits concatenating in i156), then snaps each circuit to the nearest rule-consistent table; if all re-asks fail, falls back to a consistent table instead of returning a malformed guess.
preserved_behaviors: Same relay conversation, system prompt, first-turn and per-answer wording as the parent.
Repeat-query veto and re-ask (MAX_REASKS=3, vetoed replies spend no query).
Per-circuit share cap ceil(B/3) while other circuits still need queries.
Final prompt keeps the observed table with '?' and env.last_turn_prompt; observed bits always override the model's bits; 24-bit guess / row-statement parsing and the FINAL_REASKS re-ask path.
Model writes every query; harness never chooses one. If the rules admit no table (consistent() empty) everything falls back to parent behavior.
verification: Offline: re-scored parent g0 histories with the enumerator: per-circuit candidate counts were 1 for 26/30 circuits; parent guesses were rule-inconsistent in most failing circuits.
Run 1 (final-step fix only, queries identical to parent): 7/10 exact; i156 regressed to unparsed (model wrote correct per-circuit tables but a 22-bit concatenation); i250/i239 lost a 2-way tie.

Run 2 (added per-circuit line parsing, consistent fallback, forced-answer veto, cap relaxation, early stop): check_b0r1 script -> 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, final table correct=True, circuits 3/3 on every instance; queries used 7-17 (mean 11.7); 0 crashes.

Traces: every sent query came from a model <query> reply; 1-7 forced-answer vetoes per episode, 0-1 cap vetoes, 0 format re-asks; max consecutive vetoes 1-5 (i128: 5, i247: 4 -> at least one turn burnt each); all 30 circuits fully determined at the final turn.
risks: The enumerator encodes one reading of the rules (exactly two binary gates per circuit, NOTs anywhere and stackable). If an instance's circuits fall outside it, consistent() returns {} and the harness reverts to parent behavior; a partial mismatch could snap to a wrong table.

When every circuit is determined, the final table is fixed by the bookkeeping, not by the model's fills; accuracy then depends on the model's queries covering the open rows, not on its final reasoning.

Forced-answer vetoes cost LLM calls; if the 7B keeps proposing forced rows, a turn can be burnt after 4 vetoes (observed: i128 had 5 and i247 had 4 consecutive vetoes, so each burnt at least one turn; both still ended fully determined and correct).
Only 10 instances; inventories with 2 NOTs appeared in 2 of them.
